subject: One-time margin relief and multi-year discount carveout — VP/CFO approval needed
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medivest.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: 3-yr committed + request for margin relief

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and routing controls. We're getting internal buy-in but have a hard cap from procurement on ACV and need to present a single year-1 committed price that hits margins they can sign off on.

Summary of ask:
- 3 year commitment, annual prepay (year 1 heavier)
- Asking for a 45% list discount in year 1 to meet internal budget floor
- Requesting one-time onboarding credit to offset seat-migration costs (~$50k)

I've attached our internal term sheet (Medivest_MultiYear_Term_Proposal.pdf). Can your team confirm whether this discount / one-off credit is feasible with an executive sign-off? If so, we'd like to lock before end of Q3.

Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement, Medivest Health
liam.oconnor@medivest.com

Attachments: Medivest_MultiYear_Term_Proposal.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medivest.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 3-yr committed + request for margin relief

Hi Liam — really appreciate the clear ask and the draft term sheet. Quick notes:
- We typically cap one-time onboarding credits at 20% of year-1 committed ARR, but we can consider an exception for strategic cross-region customers.
- 45% off list is outside our standard commercial guardrails for a 3-year prepay; we'll need VP/CFO approval and a short business case that justifies unit economics impact.

I'm looping in Jonas to confirm capacity (multi-region routing) and to kick off an internal exception packet. Can you confirm expected annual token volumes by year and the preferred invoicing cadence? That will help our quantitative justification.

Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-pricing-comparison.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: 3-yr committed + request for margin relief — need exec sign-off

Team — forwarding Medivest's ask. Highlights for your review:
- 3-year prepay with front-loaded year-1 (approx. 60% of total commitment)
- They are requesting a 45% list-level discount in year-1 and a one-time onboarding credit ~$50k
- Strategic: multi-region (US + EU) use, potential for marketplace listing next year (reference account for healthcare vertical)

Why I think this merits exception consideration:
- High strategic value (reference healthcare customer with multi-region needs)
- Predictable committed revenue over 3 years reduces our churn risk and gives runway to convert additional workloads on dedicated capacity

Proposed guardrails for approval packet:
1) Limit effective discount to a blended cap of 35% on year-1 (via seat/feature restrictions) unless VP/CFO approve higher.
2) One-time onboarding credit limited to $50k and only applied to year-1 invoice.
3) Include a make-good clause if usage > committed by >25% in any year (accelerated billing to preserve unit economics).

Rishi — can you run a quick NPV/unit economics delta for 35% vs 45% list discount and confirm the break-even ARR for CFO signoff?
Jonas — confirm operational feasibility for multi-region routing and any added infra cost.

Thanks — K.

On attachments: I included our pricing comp spreadsheet and the Medivest term sheet from Liam.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-23T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal: 3-yr committed + request for margin relief — need exec sign-off

Kimberly / Marissa — ran the numbers. Notes below (summary):
- At 35% blended discount in year-1, the incremental unit margin loss is ~12% relative to our baseline assumptions; NPV over 3 years remains positive given prepay structure, assuming no more than 10% churn and the projected token profile in the spreadsheet.
- At 45% discount, NPV turns negative unless we secure stronger upfront payment terms (100% prepay) or reduce support/feature entitlements.

Recommended conditional approval path:
A) Approve up to 35% blended discount + $50k onboarding credit (no additional concessions).
B) If the sales owner insists on 45%, require: 100% prepay for year-1 AND a churn escrow (20% of year-1 credit held until month 9).
C) Require an explicit operational uplift fee to cover multi-region egress/replication (estimate: $8k/mo).

I'll draft the memo for VP/CFO that shows the economics and the two-path options above. If you want me to include other levers (e.g., token caps, quantization constraints), say the word.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
